title: Opinion drift with no campaign: normal vs zealot population
question: How does voter opinion change without media and party workers over many rounds, in a normal and a zealot-included population?

manifestos.b0: optimise_manifesto on v(0) of the zealot world (round-0 optimum)
manifestos.oracle: oracle_manifesto(electorate, config): optimum on the T = 5 social-only forecast of the zealot world

metric_definitions.disagreement: mean over all voters of TV(v_i, population mean) — the XC 'spread'
metric_definitions.within: within-region spread: mean over all voters of TV(v_i, own region mean)
metric_definitions.between: between-region dispersion: PLAIN (unweighted) mean of TV over the 6 pairs of region means
metric_definitions.disagreement_free: disagreement restricted to the voters that are NOT zealots in the ζ = 0.05 world (same voter set in both populations), distance to the full population mean
metric_definitions.mean_shift: TV(population mean at t, population mean at 0)
metric_definitions.moved: mean over voters of TV(v_i(t), v_i(0))
metric_definitions.region_drift: mean over the 4 regions of TV(region mean at t, region mean at 0)
metric_definitions.E_<m>: expected vote share mean σ(β(S_i − z)), S_i = 1 − TV(v_i, b), for fixed manifesto m
metric_definitions.won_<m>: share of voters with S_i ≥ z = 0.825
metric_definitions.region_mean: per-region mean preference (4 × 5), all voters of the region (zealots included)

definitions.normal_consensus: c = Σ π_i v_i(0), π_i ∝ d_i/a_i; isolated voters keep v_i(0)
definitions.zealots_fj: Friedkin–Johnsen fixed point, zealots stubborn at v(0) (x2_stubborn.fj_solve, Jacobi-CG on the GPU, float64)

provenance.batch_layout: [2 populations, 50 worlds × N voters, 5] on one disjoint-union graph
